enhanced_information: Glucose-6 phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PDH) deficiency can lead to drug-induced oxidative stress, causing hemolytic anemia. G6PDH deficiency is a good marker of drug-induced hemolytic anemia. Lactate dehydrogenase is released from damaged red blood cells during hemolysis and can be a possible marker of hemolytic anemia, including drug-induced cases.
analysis: Glucose-6 phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PDH) deficiency is a well-known cause of drug-induced hemolytic anemia due to oxidative stress. Lactate dehydrogenase is released from damaged red blood cells during hemolysis and can also be a marker of hemolytic anemia. While lactate dehydrogenase is a more general marker of hemolysis, G6PDH deficiency specifically links to drug-induced hemolytic anemia.
